subject: Waiting: final NPPA notification of the 30% trade-margin cap on cancer medicines
why: On 8 Oct 2026 the NPPA approved in principle a 30% cap on trade margins (of MRP) for non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines, expected to cut their retail prices by 20–70%; a DGHS expert committee is to finalise the list of medicines before NPPA notifies it. A draft is not a rule. Each run, check NPPA/PIB for the final notification and list. Once notified, check which of Beta Drugs' (and other covered pharma companies') brands are on the list, correct the notes, reconsider the call, then mark this handled. 16 Oct 2026: no final notification yet (reports say the DGHS list covers about 110 drugs). 18 Oct 2026: press reports (Tribune, ETV Bharat, Medical Dialogues, 17 Oct) say the NPPA issued the final order, Gazette S.O. 5690(E) of 17 Oct 2026, capping trade margins at 30% for 137 non-scheduled cancer drugs (including patented ones and direct hospital supply), with lower MRPs from 9 Nov 2026 based on March 2026 net sales realisation. Reported list includes pemetrexed, abiraterone, azacitidine, anastrozole, erlotinib, sunitinib, everolimus, bevacizumab and many newer patented drugs, but not bortezomib, capecitabine, imatinib, temozolomide, docetaxel, gemcitabine, paclitaxel, oxaliplatin or the platinum drugs. The official NPPA, Gazette and Department of Pharmaceuticals sites could not be reached from this session, so the order is not yet confirmed from the source; next run, confirm it and check Beta Drugs', Natco's and Shilpa Medicare's exposure to the listed molecules. 21 Oct 2026: more outlets (ThePrint, Business Today, Moneylife, PTI) confirm a Gazette notification of 17 Oct covering 137 formulations, new prices from 9 Nov, makers to report revised prices within 7 days and keep production levels. The NPPA, Gazette and Department of Pharmaceuticals sites still could not be reached (no response or 503), and PIB has no release on it, so it is still not confirmed from the source. 23 Oct 2026: Deccan Chronicle and Upstox also report the 30% cap on 137 formulations from 9 Nov under paragraph 19 of the DPCO; NPPA and Gazette sites still give no response from this session, so not confirmed from the source. 25 Oct 2026: All India Radio (newsonair.gov.in, 19 Oct) also reports the cap on 137 formulations from 9 Nov under paragraph 19 of the DPCO, but the NPPA and Gazette sites still give no response from this session, so the order itself is not yet read. 28 Oct 2026: still only press and All India Radio reports (137 drugs, lower MRPs from 9 Nov 2026); the NPPA and Gazette sites still cannot be reached from this session, so the order itself has not been read. 30 Oct 2026: still no final notification seen; on its 22 Oct call Beta said the cap would have negligible impact on it (orals sold through distributors; most injectables already price-controlled). 1 Nov 2026: no final NPPA notification in the digests; Jupiter Life Line’s Q2 call (26 Oct) said a cap is to apply from 1 November, unconfirmed; left open. 4 Nov 2026: news of 3 Nov reports that NPPA cut the maximum retail prices of 1,085 anti-cancer medicines; this may be the final notification. Confirm it against NPPA's order next run (see also the HCG waiting entry); left open. 8 Nov 2026: no final NPPA notification of the trade-margin cap in the filings or news digests to 7 November; left open. 15 Nov 2026: no final NPPA notification in the filings or news digests to 14 November; left open.
